nodes.name: Core-shell ZIF synthesis and pyrolysis
nodes.procedure: Core-shell ZIF-8@ZIF-67 chosen as precursor and pyrolyzed to generate hollow polyhedral porous carbon with Co nanoparticle supported (Co_n@NPC), where the evaporated Zn in ZIF-8 isolates contiguous Co atoms to form uniform Co crystal during the pyrolysis process. N-pointed cavities created by Zn evaporation and Co aggregation. Appropriate pyrolysis temperature, pyrolysis time, and Co/Zn mole ratio necessary for uniform growth of Co nanoparticles.
nodes.source_text: Firstly, we chose core-shell ZIF-8@ZIF-67[16] as a precursor... to generate hollow polyhedral porous carbon with Co nanoparticle supported (Co_n@NPC)... It is worth mentioning that the appropriate pyrolysis temperature (Figure S35-36), pyrolysis time (Figure S37-38), and Co/Zn mole ratio (Figure S39-41) are necessary for the uniform growth of Co nanoparticles.

unit_operations.procedure_snippet: pyrolyzed to generate hollow polyhedral porous carbon with Co nanoparticle supported

nodes.name: Pt impregnation and confinement
nodes.procedure: Co_n@NPC was impregnated in an H2PtCl6 solution to capture free [PtCl6]2- ions, accompanied by confining Pt atoms in N-pointed cavities through Pt-N coordination at 60°C. The facile low-temperature treatment avoids the accumulation of Pt atoms, and the design of the core-shell structure also protects Pt1 from dissolution. Additionally, driven by the difference in reduction potentials between the Co and Pt ions, galvanic replacement reaction occurs simultaneously.

Even at 100 mAcm^{-2}, the overpotential of Co_n-Pt_1@NPC (91 mV) in alkali is only half that of Pt/C (178 mV)... shows no obvious decay after a long period of 100 h in alkaline (Figure 4e).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM and TEM confirm individual Pt atoms coexist with Co nanoparticles; lattice fringes of Co_n remain unchanged after Pt introduction, showing 0.175 nm assigned to Co(200) plane; Co diameter reduced from ~26 nm to ~16 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In aberration-corrected high-angle annular darkfield scanning transmission electron microscope (HAADF-STEM) images, individual Pt atoms coexist with Co nanoparticles (Figure 2i). Figure 2j demonstrates that Pt atoms mainly fall on the carbon surface. Moreover, the lattice fringes of Co_n remain unchanged after Pt introduction, showing a clear lattice fringe of 0.175 nm assigned to the (200) plane

nodes.characterization_summary: Atomically dispersed Pt sites homogeneously surround Co_n nanoparticles in Co_n-Pt_1@NPC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The STEM-coupled EDS element mapping also reveals that the atomically dispersed Pt sites homogeneously surround Co_n (Figure 2l and Figure S25).

nodes.characterization_summary: No diffraction peaks for bulk Pt; Co crystal diffractions resolved confirming metallic Co nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: there is no diffraction associated with bulk Pt whereas Co crystal diffractions are resolved on X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns (Figure 2m and Figure S26).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt 4f spectra deconvoluted into Pt2+ and Pt4+ states; Pt2+ shows 0.30 eV negative shift in Co_n-Pt_1@NPC vs Pt_1@NPC indicating electron accumulation on Pt; Co 2p shows positive shifts for Co-Nx and metallic Co peaks; N 1s shows increased metal-N proportion after Pt loading.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Pt 4f spectra of Co_n+c-Pt_1@NPC (Figure S43), Pt_1@NPC, and Co_n-Pt_1@NPC (Figure 3a) are deconvoluted into two pairs of peaks, indicating that two oxidation states for Pt species (+2 and +4) exist ... Compared to Pt_1@NPC free of Co_n, a negative shift of 0.30 eV is observed on Pt2+ in Co_n-Pt_1@NPC

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L3-edge XANES shows Pt oxidation state between Pt foil and PtO2 consistent with XPS; Co K-edge XANES reflects dominant metallic Co properties.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As revealed in Pt L3 edge XANES spectra, Pt in Co_n-Pt_1@NPC shows an oxidation state between Pt foil and PtO2 (Figure 3d), consistent with XPS results ... Co K-edge XANES also reflects the dominant metal properties of Co (Figure 3g).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L3-edge FT-EXAFS shows prominent Pt-C/N peak at 1.60 Å, no Pt-Pt (2.54 Å), Pt-O (1.67 Å), or Pt-Co (2.2 Å) peaks; wavelet transform confirms Pt-N at k=7.5 Å⁻¹, R=1.60 Å; fitting shows Pt-N bond length 2.01 Å, CN=3.9; Co K-edge FT-EXAFS shows Co-Co at 2.08 Å, average CN=5.5.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Co_n-Pt_1@NPC displays a prominent peak at 1.60Å originating from the Pt-C/N vector (Figure 3e) and no Pt-Pt (2.54Å) and Pt-O (1.67Å) vectors are observed ... quantitative EXAFS fitting corroborates that Pt1 is directly coordinated with four N atoms with bond lengths of 2.01Å, with coordination number approximately 3.9 ... The FT-EXAFS spectrum shows only one dominant peak at 2.08Å, corresponding to the scattering of Co-Co bonds ... The average C.N. of Co-Co reaches 5.5
